pieces.title: TEST Delaware corporation, Delaware LLC or Wyoming LLC: what each pays every year

slides.title: Delaware corporation, Delaware LLC or Wyoming LLC: what each pays every year
Delaware corporation
slides.body: Delaware corporations file their annual report and pay franchise tax, a yearly state tax, by 1 March each year. The annual report fee is $50 for a corporation that is not exempt, and $25 for an exempt one.

slides.title: Franchise tax by authorized shares
slides.body: Authorized shares are the most shares your charter allows. Under the Authorized Shares method, 5,000 shares or fewer pay the minimum $175, 5,001 to 10,000 shares pay $250, and each further 10,000 shares or part of them adds $85.

slides.title: Or by assumed par value capital
slides.body: The Assumed Par Value Capital method has a $400 minimum and needs the corporation's issued shares and total gross assets. Delaware's page says: "Use the method that results in the lesser tax."

slides.title: Delaware LLC
slides.body: A Delaware LLC pays an annual tax of $400, due by 1 June for the year before.

slides.title: Wyoming LLC
slides.body: A Wyoming LLC's annual report is due on the first day of the month it was formed in, every year. Wyoming's annual license tax is $60, or $0.0002 for each dollar of the company's assets located and employed in Wyoming, whichever is greater.

pieces.title: TEST Foreign owned US LLC? Form 5472 and the $25,000 penalty

content.hook: Is your US LLC owned entirely by one foreign person?
lines: If it is not taxed as a corporation, it files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120, a corporate return filed as a formality.
That is for each year it has a reportable transaction with a related party, such as its owner.
For 2026, that pro forma 1120 with Form 5472 is due by Thursday 15 April 2027.
Form 7004 extends the time to file by six months, to Friday 15 October 2027.
This Form 5472 cannot be filed electronically: it is faxed to 855-887-7737 or mailed to the IRS in Ogden, Utah.
Not filing a required Form 5472 on time carries a $25,000 penalty.
Another $25,000 follows for each 30 days, or part of 30 days, that the failure continues more than 90 days after the IRS's notice.

pieces.title: TEST Beneficial ownership reports in 2026: who still files

content.text: US companies and US persons do not report beneficial ownership information to FinCEN; a final rule made this permanent from 14 August 2026.

captions.facebook:
Beneficial ownership reports in 2026: who still files?

Beneficial ownership information is about who owns or controls a company. US companies and US persons do not report it to FinCEN, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network; a final rule made this permanent from 14 August 2026.

Certain companies formed outside the US and registered to do business in a US state still report it, leaving out any US person owners, within 30 days of notice that their registration is effective.

pieces.title: TEST 506(b) or 506(c): can you post about your raise?

content.hook: 506(b) or 506(c): can you post about your raise?
lines: Under Rule 506(b), a company cannot use general solicitation or advertising, meaning promoting the raise to the public.
It can sell to any number of accredited investors plus up to 35 other purchasers who are financially sophisticated, alone or with a representative.
An individual can be an accredited investor through the SEC's income, net worth or license tests.
Under Rule 506(c), a company can advertise its raise broadly.
But every purchaser must be accredited, and the company must take reasonable steps to verify it, such as reviewing tax returns or bank statements.

pieces.title: TEST Who counts as an accredited investor

slides.title: Who counts as an accredited investor
By income
slides.body: An individual is an accredited investor with income over $200,000, or over $300,000 with a spouse or spousal equivalent, in each of the last two years, and reasonably expects the same this year.

slides.title: By net worth
slides.body: An individual also qualifies with a net worth over $1 million, alone or with a spouse or spousal equivalent, not counting their primary residence.

slides.title: By a professional license
slides.body: An individual also qualifies by holding a Series 7, 65 or 82 license in good standing.

pieces.title: TEST What a late or wrong 1099 costs

content.hook: What does a late or wrong 1099 cost?
lines: Forms 1099-NEC for 2026 payments go to each payee and to the IRS by Monday 1 February 2027.
A 1099 due in 2027 that is late or wrong costs $60 a return if put right within 30 days of the due date.
It costs $130 a return if put right by 1 August, and $340 after that or if never filed.
Intentional disregard, ignoring the rules on purpose, costs at least $690 a return.
A late or wrong payee copy, the one for the person you paid, is penalized separately on the same scale.
